text: We saw earlier that the matrix $ \left[\begin{array}{rrr} 4 \amp 2 \amp 3 \\ 0 \amp -2 \amp -1 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 3 \\ \end{array}\right] $ has the characteristic equation $$(4-\lambda)(-2-\lambda)(3-\lambda)=0$$ . There are three eigenvalues $\lambda=3,-2,1$ each having multiplicity $1$. By the proposition, we are guaranteed that the dimension of each eigenspace is $1$; that is, $$ \dim E_3 = \dim E_{-2} = \dim E_1 = 1 $$ . It turns out that this is enough to guarantee that there is a basis of $\real^3$ consisting of eigenvectors.
